answer: We model Sybil identity multiplication as an adversarial ripple across pseudonymous agents, where each spawned identity must forge a dynamic opportunity-cost bond scaled to marginal consensus rent; subgame-perfect punishment matrices then slash bonded capital upon detected equivocation, rendering deviation strictly dominated. A sable equilibrium condition follows: expected payoff per identity is negative whenever bond exceeds discounted fork value, so no profitable multi-agent deviation exists and honest participation is the unique strict Nash equilibrium.
